metadata.case_name: WONG CHI KWONG v. POLYTRADE RECYCLING (HK) LTD

plaintiff.occupation_before: general labour in the Defendant’s plastics recycling factory
plaintiff.expected_occupation_after: lighter and more sedentary jobs such as salesman in lighter goods, gas station worker, fast food stall worker or security guard

injuries.description: Multiple open wounds in his left groin (4 cm), left thigh (8 cm) and left calf (15 cm).
injuries.body_part: left lower limb (left groin, left thigh, left calf)
source: He sustained crush injury to his left lower limb which resulted in multiple open wounds in his left groin (4 cm), left thigh (8 cm) and left calf (15 cm).
injuries.icd_description: Multiple open wounds of lower leg

source: the wounds were heavily contaminated with tear of soleus and gastrocenemius and contusion of posterior tibial nerve.
injuries.icd_description: Laceration of other muscle, fascia or tendon of posterior muscle group at lower leg level

source: the wounds were heavily contaminated with tear of soleus and gastrocenemius and contusion of posterior tibial nerve.
injuries.icd_description: Injury of tibial nerve at lower leg level

injuries.description: evidence of sciatic nerve crash injury
source: There was also evidence of sciatic nerve crash injury and left knee lateral collateral ligament avulsion.
injuries.icd_description: Injury of sciatic nerve at hip or thigh level

injuries.description: left knee lateral collateral ligament avulsion
source: There was also evidence of sciatic nerve crash injury and left knee lateral collateral ligament avulsion.
injuries.icd_description: Rupture of lateral collateral ligament of knee

source: There were multiple open wounds to his left groin, left thigh and left calf, with fracture of his left fibula.

injuries.description: left peroneal nerve palsy (partial recovery; further neurological recovery cannot be expected)
injuries.body_part: left peroneal nerve / left ankle motor function
source: electrophysiological study done on the Plaintiff revealed residual absent sensory and motor response of left peroneal nerve of regeneration.
Dr. Lau stated in his report that the Plaintiff has partial recovery from the left peroneal nerve palsy.
Dr. Lau opined that further neurological recovery of the left peroneal nerve palsy cannot be expected. It is expected that the motor weakness of the Plaintiff’s left lower limb is to be permanent.
injuries.icd_description: Injury of peroneal nerve at lower leg level

injuries.description: extensive and multiple scars over his left lower limb
source: Examination also revealed extensive and multiple scars over the Plaintiff’s left lower limb.
The Plaintiff was also left with extensive scarrings over his left lower limb which is disturbing to him.

manifestations.description: numbness and pain in his left leg, circumferentially from the knee down to the ankle and then involving the dorsal and plantar aspects of the foot

the pain and numbness was intermittent in nature and was associated with getting up from the seat after sitting for about 2 hours; walking for half an hour; standing for more than an hour; squatting for 5 minutes; getting up from the squatting position; climbing 2 flights of stairs
could walk normally but he could not squat fully
difficulty with walking on heels and could not stand in a stable manner on his left leg alone
loss of active dorsiflexion of his left ankle
weakness of the dorsiflexion and eversion of the Plaintiff’s left ankle
a small area of mild degree of touch sensation loss over the lateral aspect of the left lower leg
generalized motor weakness of his left lower limb when first referred to the clinic in January 2005
foot drop deformity (neurological recovery was evidenced by improvement in the foot drop deformity)
extensive and multiple scars over the Plaintiff’s left lower limb (observed on physical examination)

treatments_received: MRI to define extent of deep abscess and sinus (28 February 2005)
wide excision of the sinus and abscess (28 February 2005)
neurolysis of the sciatic nerve (28 February 2005)
occupational therapy: work reconditioning and hardening programme (13 sessions since April 2006)

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: Prior to the accident, he used to play badminton, table tennis, soccer and basketball. He could no longer enjoy these activities and sports after the accident.
Extensive scarrings over his left lower limb which is disturbing to him.
Difficulty in negotiating uneven surfaces; could only stand for about an hour; could not stand in a stable manner on his left leg alone; difficulty with walking on heels.

Would have difficulty in returning to his pre-injury job in the plastic recycling factory which involved a lot of heavy manual work such as lifting heavy bags of plastic waste and standing for a long period of time.
